maya: Ran an A100 vs H100 sweep with real traffic slice for the 7B family. Quick TL;DR: H100 wins low-batch decode latency, A100 edges on throughput for large-batch int8 runs. Cost-ish numbers (rough) below, full charts + CSV in s3: https://s3.redwood-internal/prod-bench/2033500000/chart.png :chart_with_upwards_trend:

sam: Nice. what exact configs? batch sizes / seq lengths?

maya: batches = [1,4,16], prefills = [128,512], decode = 256 tokens. Models: raven-7b, llama-7b-open, vicuna-7b. Quant modes: fp16, q4f, int8_ptq. Regions: us-west1 (A100), us-central1 (H100).

maya: Bench command we used (benchmark harness):
```
./bench --model=raven-7b --device=auto --profile=prefill_decode --batch=[1,4,16] --prefill=[128,512] --decode=256 --quant=[fp16,q4f,int8_ptq] --kernel-policy=auto --traffic-sample=samples/real_1h.json
```

eli: Which kernel backends? TRT for hopper? driver/torch versions?

maya: For H100 we forced TensorRT-backed casting for decode paths (--kernel-policy=tensorrt). For A100 we used cuBLASLt optimized kernels (--kernel-policy=cublaslt) because TRT for that SKU regressed on some attention shapes. CUDA 12.3, TRT 8.8.1, pytorch 2.2.

tina: Numbers pls — latency / tokens/sec / $/1M tokens.

maya: Paste of condensed table from CSV (median values across runs):
Model | HW | batch | prefill | median prefill ms | median decode ms | tok/s | $/1M toks
raven-7b | H100 | 1 | 128 | 120 | 18 | 2100 | $270
raven-7b | A100 | 1 | 128 | 150 | 22 | 1800 | $315
raven-7b | H100 | 16 | 512 | 520 | 95 | 5200 | $110
raven-7b | A100 | 16 | 512 | 560 | 89 | 5400 | $125
(above costs assume on-demand per-GPU rental: H100 $3.2/hr, A100 $3.8/hr, normalized to token throughput and including 10% infra overhead)

maya: Notes: int8_ptq increased tok/s ~15% on A100 at batch16 but added 2.8% eval regressions on our quality set; q4f gave ~7% perf boost with <1% quality delta. H100 TRT decode latencies were consistently ~10-20% lower at batch1 and batch4.

sam: Did you run KV cache warm/cold scenarios?

maya: Yep — main runs were warm-cache (simulates interactive). Cold-cache increases prefill by ~30-40% on both SKUs; relative H100 advantage holds.

eli: Any kernel fallbacks observed in logs?

maya: One TRT kernel fallback on raven-7b int8 in us-central (single run) due to small-tensor layout; bench-bot captured it: "bench-bot: run 2033500005: TRT kernel fallback -> cublaslt fallback invoked"

bench-bot: benchmark run 2033500005 completed (logs: https://s3.redwood-internal/prod-bench/2033500000/run2033500005.log)

tina: For the quality regressions you saw on int8_ptq can you paste the example prompts that regressed?

maya: Short list (shared gist): https://gist.github.com/redwood/2033500000-int8-regressions. Summary: majority were numerical hallucinations and altered tokenization in a few edge system prompts. We'll add these to the eval regression dashboard.

sam: Great. next steps? multi-region failover? pricing sensitivity?

maya: Plan: 1) Run multi-region crosszone tests (us-west + europe-west) next week, 2) repeat with more recent TRT 8.9 once infra image updates, 3) run larger-family (13B) sanity run for a single config. I'll drop full CSV and perf notebook in the s3 folder by EOD.

eli: +1. Can you add a small script that converts tok/s -> $/1M tokens so product can play with pricing?

maya: Will do. I'll post it in the folder. :white_check_mark:
